text: The Patriots are bracing for Week 2 against the Steelers without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who has been downgraded to out after being listed as questionable, though there's better news in the backfield where TreVeyon Henderson—who missed the opener with an ankle injury—proclaimed himself "ready to go" and is expected to return to action. The team will lean on elevated punter Mitch Wishnowsky for the second consecutive week as they look to bounce back, while Pittsburgh will also be hampered by injuries with starting wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined by a foot injury. In a bittersweet moment off the field, legendary cornerback Stephon Gilmore—a two-time All-Pro and the NFL's 2019 Defensive Player of the Year—signed a one-day contract to retire as a Patriot on Friday, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest defensive backs in franchise history. Meanwhile, owner Robert Kraft made headlines this week by having rapper Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium shows, citing the artist's "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery" that Kraft felt was offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.
